sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that while the primary atonement through kindness draws down the inner will, the nullification of defects requires a drawing down from the Essence of Ein Sof, which is separate from will, achieved through elevation.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that this which is brought above
(section 5)
that the primary atonement is acts of kindness because the innermost will of Above is in drawing down below,
"I desire kindness,"
is primarily regarding that there should be satisfaction before Him, blessed be He,
and also regarding the correction of defects.
But regarding the nullification of defects
[for this matter is because the Essence of Ein Sof, the Possessor of will, is separate from the will],
there is an advantage in the drawing down that is connected to elevation.
For through elevation
(going out of one's existence,
nullification)
one reaches this matter in the Possessor of will that is separate from the will.
And through the drawing down that follows the elevation, this matter
(that Ein Sof is separate from the will)
is drawn down below,
and through this the defects are nullified.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two aspects of "Ki Tisa" — lifting the head and raising the horn of Israel — correspond to simple kindness and the kindness of prayer, and Moshe's question about raising the horn relates to drawing from the Essence of Ein Sof, which is separate from will.

translations.translation: And this is "When you lift up the head of the children of Israel etc." And it is brought in the Gemara: Moshe said before the Holy One, blessed be He, "Master of the Universe, with what will You raise the horn of Israel?" He said to him, "With 'Ki Tisa' (when you lift up)."
It can be said that the two matters in "Ki Tisa" — the lifting and raising of the head of the children of Israel and the raising of the horn of Israel —
are analogous to the two matters of kindness,
simple kindness and the kindness of prayer.
And the explanation is,
that the weakness
(descent and degradation)
caused by the sin in the head of the soul,
that it is unable to illuminate the inner powers,
is analogous to the withdrawal of light that occurs due to the defect,
that the light departs to its source and does not illuminate the vessels.
And the matter of the lifting and raising of the head
[that the power of revelation of the aspect of the head in the soul is in full force as it was originally,
to illuminate the inner powers]
which is effected by giving a ransom for charity, is analogous to the atonement
(filling the defects and restoring the will)
effected by simple acts of kindness.
And Moshe's question was, "With what will You raise the horn of Israel?"
For since the descent in the level of the horn is
(not that the sin caused a descent in it,
but rather)
that the intention for which it descended below was not fulfilled,
Moshe wondered how this could be rectified.
And it can be said,
that this that Moshe said before the Holy One, blessed be He, "With what will You raise the horn of Israel?"
is because in order to rectify this, that the intention was not fulfilled, it is through the drawing down from the Essence of Ein Sof, the Possessor of will, who is separate from the will,
and therefore Moshe said this before the Holy One, blessed be He, who is holy and separate,
and moreover,
"before the Holy One, blessed be He,"
in order to draw down from there.
He said to him, "With 'Ki Tisa' (when you lift up),"
in that Moshe will lift their head in elevation,
for even the drawing down of the aspect of "before the Holy One, blessed be He" must be through the aspect of wisdom
(the matter of Moshe),
and analogous to the known principle that even the revelation of the Surrounding is through the Filling.
And even though the action of Moshe
(from his own side)
is "when you lift up the head,"
nevertheless, through this is also drawn the power of the aspect of "before the Holy One, blessed be He,"
through which the raising of the horn of Israel is effected.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the lifting of the head through Moshe taking a ransom for charity draws down the Essence of Ein Sof, which is separate from will, thereby raising the horn of Israel in honor.

translations.translation: And in order that this matter be drawn down to Israel, it is through that their lifting and raising of the head is by Moshe taking from them a ransom,
as Rashi's wording: "Take from them a ransom for charity,"
the matter of the elevation that is in charity.
And analogous to what is explained above
(section 7),
that through simple kindness there is a drawing down of the will from the Possessor of will,
and in order to reach this matter in the Possessor of will that is separate from the will, it is through the kindness of prayer,
a drawing down that is connected to elevation,
similarly is it regarding the matter of the ransom of his soul,
that through giving the ransom for charity
(drawing down)
there is a drawing down of the will,
and through this the lifting and raising of the head is effected.
And through that Moshe takes from them a ransom for charity
(the matter of the elevation that is in charity)
there is a drawing down of the Essence of Ein Sof that is separate from the will,
and through this the horn of Israel is raised,
in the manner of "his horn
shall be raised in honor."
